show_hn.title: Show HN: Automatic deduction of FlashAttention kernel from ~25 lines of SQL
show_hn.story_text:
In this demo, we automatically deduce a FlashAttention kernel with ~25 lines of SQL, which just expresses vanilla attention. This is possible due to three portable SQL extensions that we’re building:
- xarray-sql: a library that efficiently represents petabyte scale array datasets in the cloud as tables (relations).
- ddx: a database extension that adds automatic differentiation in the style of JAX to standard SQL, assuming the above array data model.
- einfold: a modular query planner for fast tensor contractions in vanilla SQL, again, assuming the above array data model. My hope is that the relational model and algebra provide fresh perspectives on how we might do accelerator programming. Here, our thesis is that separating the logical layers in a tensor program from the physical layers

We’re happy to introduce Artificer, our first robotics decision model for evaluating robot task progress and success.
The problem
Robot systems need feedback during training, evaluation, and deployment. An arm might grasp the right object, but place it in the wrong bin. A robot might’ve only completed part of its task before it stopped. Assessing these outcomes from video often requires manual review or brittle, handcrafted objectives. Though frontier models do well in evaluation, they are expensive and slow. 
Artificer is a 4B parameter model that estimates task completion and progress, at the frontier level, from a task description and video. During deployment, these estimates provide feedback to a robot controller to help decide whether to continue an attempt, retry, or move to the next

show_hn.story_text: I built a news article bias detector tool. You paste the link of any article into it and it will give the article a bias rating from 1 - 7. It scores based on loaded wording in the article, the acknowledgement of different perspectives and if they're justified. show_hn.title: Show HN: HackerFlow – A Responsive HN Reader
show_hn.story_text:
A lot of people love hacker news because the website is simple, fast, and its UI stays out of the way. I just can't seem to leave well enough alone I built HackerFlow because I wanted to browse HN visually while keeping articles and comments in the same place.The goal is a fast UI that stays out of the way but offers more visuals. I tried a few other GUIs and none of them really satisfied me. Features: - Gallery, magazine, list and compact views
- Inline article reader with rendered text and page previews
- Infinite scrolling with thumbnail preloading
- Collapsible comments, capped indentation and next-parent navigation
- Preserved scroll position when opening stories or navigating back
- Search, local bookmarks, dark mode and keyboard shortcuts
- Responsive layouts and an installable
